summary: Colonsay Airstrip is a small grass-runway airport serving the Isle of Colonsay, a remote and sparsely populated Inner Hebridean island off Scotland's west coast. The airstrip provides a vital transport link for residents and visitors, connecting the island to the Scottish mainland via scheduled Loganair flights. Its single short runway accommodates only small twin-engine aircraft, making it one of the more challenging yet scenic air links in the British Isles.
faqs:
Q: Who operates flights to Colonsay Airstrip?
A: Loganair operates scheduled flights primarily to and from Oban on the Scottish mainland.

Q: How long is the runway at Colonsay?
A: The runway is a short grass strip approximately 500 metres in length, suitable only for light aircraft.

Q: Are there any airport facilities at Colonsay Airstrip?
A: Facilities are minimal, typical of a remote island airstrip, with no terminal building of note and limited services.

Q: Can private aircraft land at Colonsay?
A: Yes, prior permission is recommended for private or charter flights due to the limited infrastructure.
transport_tips: Taxis or pre-arranged hire cars meet arriving flights, as public transport on Colonsay is very limited. The ferry terminal at Scalasaig is only a short drive from the airstrip, useful for onward connections to other Hebridean islands. Booking ground transport in advance is strongly advised, especially outside summer months.
local_tip: Sit on the left side of the aircraft when flying into Colonsay for a spectacular approach view over the island's varied terrain and the surrounding turquoise Hebridean waters.
